question: to the Commission Damien Carême (The Left), Manon Aubry (The Left), Anthony Smith (The Left), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Rima Hassan (The Left) Subject:

The United States and Israel are intensifying their unlawful military interventions against the leadership of oil-producing nations worldwide, targeting Venezuela in January and, since February, Iran. On 18 March 2026, Eurostat reported that the Union remains highly dependent on energy imports. The following day, it emerged that the majority of EU Member States generate less than 50% of their energy from renewable sources, despite the fact that only a transition to renewable energy can guarantee our independence. The consequences of war and our dependence have a direct impact on our economies and on the purchasing power of European citizens. The insecurity and risks weighing on the Strait of Hormuz are prompting oil groups to speculate, leading to a sharp surge in diesel prices at the pump across Europe. 1.
Does the Commission continue to regard the United States and Israel as allies despite their ongoing breaches of international law?
Will it take steps to freeze the price of diesel in order to prevent a spike in prices for European citizens?
What policies will it finally implement to extricate the European Union from its dependence on fossil fuels and mitigate its vulnerability to the unpredictability of President Trump's imperialism?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.5.2026) The US is a strategic partner of the EU. The transatlantic partnership is founded on a shared history and strong bonds. The EU will continue to work to maintain close engagement with the US as it is beneficial to EU citizens, as well as global stability and security. The EU is ready to continue engaging constructively on all issues of common interest while still defending its priorities, interests and values, including the defence of international law and the rules-based order. The EU has consistently underlined that Israel has the right to defend itself, but in line with international law, including international humanitarian law. Disproportionate use of force against civilians and civilian infrastructure is unacceptable. The AccelerateEU Communication adopted on 22 April 20261 follows a two-pronged approach to bring immediate relief to vulnerable households and industries, while advancing measures to end structural dependence on imported fossil fuels, in line with our long-term objectives. To help Member States protect consumers from price shocks, the Commission will assist in the design of immediate but targeted, temporary measures including price intervention, income support schemes and tax incentives. This will avoid market distortions while addressing the root causes of high prices and it will also facilitate the coordination of national action. The Commission’s long-term strategy is focused on electrification based on homegrown clean energy, resilient grids, flexibility, interconnections and energy efficiency reducing fossil dependence and external vulnerability. The AccelerateEU Communication calls for faster implementation of the Energy Union agenda2, with coordinated EU action and full delivery by Member States.
